thread:
perf-bot: NIGHTLY ALERT: latency P75 up +32% on model-x in us-west-2 vs baseline. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/nightly/models/model-x

maria: ugh, saw this in my morning check. looks like the spike started right after the 03:10 deploy window.
aj: which deploy? any recent kernel or batching PRs merged to main?
maria: two merges yesterday: PR#4821 dynamic-kernel-router and PR#4890 adaptive-batching-window. both landed ~02:58.
sam: paging the CI perf run: infra-ci, can you correlate the failing job?
infra-ci: CI job nightly-perf-1687 shows throughput drop and latency tail increase. Regression reproduced on the CI perf VM at 03:05. Logs: `perf/summary.json` attached to job.
lee: I pulled the profiling traces from the failing CI run. KV cache miss rate jumped from 2% -> 12% under the same trace set. That aligns with more recompute and longer kernels selected.
kira: interesting — dynamic-kernel-router switches to a wider attention kernel when activating kv cache misses because sequence lengths vary; maybe routing stability is oscillating.
aj: can you paste the kernel decision snippet?
lee: here, truncated:```json
{"step": 1200, "selected_kernel": "wide_attn_optimized", "kv_hit": false, "latency_ms": 48}
{"step": 1201, "selected_kernel": "narrow_attn_fast", "kv_hit": true, "latency_ms": 22}
```
lee: you can see flip-flop every few requests.
maria: flip-flop + higher miss rate == thrash in the KV cache LRU buckets. adaptive-batching may be increasing window sizes so requests group differently, making prefix reuse less likely.
aj: hypothesis: adaptive-batching enlarged batch windows so different sequence prefixes are coalesced, evicting hot KV entries before reuse. combined with kernel router instability -> extra compute.
perf-bot: Note: rollouts open for the two PRs. dynamic-kernel-router currently at 40% rollout; adaptive-batching-window at 60%.
releaseman: HOLD the dynamic-kernel-router rollout immediately? we should pause both until we triage.
maria: agree on pausing dynamic-kernel-router to be conservative. can we throttle adaptive-batching back to previous defaults remotely?
infra-ci: I can revert rollout flags for dynamic-kernel-router now: `rollout set dynamic-kernel-router=0` executed.
releaseman: thanks. adaptive-batching -> reduce window from 200ms to 50ms? who owns the config?
kira: I can push a config delta to lower adaptive-window to 50ms, but want to run canary (5%) first.
sam: while that's happening, let's run a quick bisect on the PRs merged last 48h. maria, can you list commits/merge SHAs?
maria: PR#4821 merge commit: `a3f5b9c` ; PR#4890 merge commit: `c7d2f1a` ; also small perf-tweak PR#4883 `d4e113f` (KV eviction heuristic change) merged earlier.
aj: that KV eviction PR might be more directly implicated. eviction heuristic delta: changed `lru_score` decay from 0.8 -> 0.5 which makes evict more aggressively.
lee: oh, that would explain the increased KV miss rate independent of batching. if LRU decay is lower, hot keys get evicted sooner when mixed traffic hits.
kira: combined effects plausible: eviction heuristic + larger batches + kernel routing oscillation => thrash.
sam: prioritize a revert of PR#4883 (d4e113f) on night cluster and re-run the perf job.
infra-ci: scheduling a canary revert on a dedicated night cluster now. will post results in ~10m.
perf-bot: CI: canary revert job started (job id 5209). expectation: p75 latency drop if eviction was the main culprit.
lee: also adding a microprofile run with `--trace-kv-liveness` to capture eviction timeline. command: `./perf_run --suite nightly --trace-kv-liveness`
maria: if revert fixes perf, we still need followups: add regression tests for kv hit-rate under mixed batching and kernel switches.
aj: and add guardrails to kernel-router decision hysteresis. maybe require 3 consecutive samples before switching kernel.
kira: good call. I'll open follow-up PRs: hysteresis on router + revert PR for eviction.
releaseman: for rollout policy: make dynamic-kernel-router default target 0 until we have hysteresis. adaptive-batching back to conservative defaults.
infra-ci: canary revert job finished: p75 down -28% vs failing run; KV miss rate back to 3%.
perf-bot: ALERT RESOLVED - metrics trending back to baseline after KV eviction revert and rollout pause.
sam: great. next steps: 1) revert merged to main? 2) implement hysteresis + tests 3) perf job to validate before re-rolling.
maria: I'll create a postmortem note in #incidents after we finish PRs. keep this thread for rollouts and perf logs.
lee: attaching microprofile excerpt:
[evict] t=162.341 key=K_12 lru=0.49 reason=score_below_threshold
[kv-miss] t=162.342 req=R_3041 prefix=abc
[router] decided wide_attn_optimized confidence=0.48
lee: thanks everyone. I'll continue collecting traces and will ping when I have a PR for router hysteresis. :thumbsup:
releaseman: moving to postmortem and follow-ups. closing the active rollout tickets. :white_check_mark:
